items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law and the social services law, in
relation to housing navigation services for those with intellectual and
developmental disabilities
items.lawCode: Add §13.44, amd §5.07, Ment Hyg L; amd §366, Soc Serv L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4469

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law and the social services law, in
relation to housing navigation services for those with intellectual and
developmental disabilities

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To assist individuals in finding appropriate housing that meets their
specific housing goals and develop individualized housing action plans.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

The bill would establish housing navigation as a service in New York's
developmental disabilities sector and require the Commissioner of the
New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OWPDD)
to develop a housing navigation training curriculum, oversee the imple-
mentation of such curriculum, and provide statewide training to individ-
uals for the provision of housing navigation services. This bill would
also require the Commissioner of the New York State Department of Health
(DOH) in consultation with the Commissioner of OPWDD, to submit the
appropriate waivers, including but not limited to, those authorized
pursuant to section eleven hundred fifteen of the federal social securi-
ty act, in order to achieve the purposes of high-quality housing coun-
seling a population of persons with developmental disabilities.

Further, this bill would require the Commissioner of OPWDD to establish
a housing navigation task force to perform tasks that will help to
ensure the successful implementation of housing navigation services
established by this section. The taskforce shall be co-chaired by the:
the Commissioner of OPWDD or his or her designee, the Commissioner of
the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA) or his or her
designee, and a representative of the New York State Homes and Community
Renewal. Ensuring adequate geographic representation, an additional ten
individuals shall be selected for the taskforce. Such individuals shall
have professional experience in the fields of affordable housing devel-
opment, banking, financial planning, and non-profit providers with expe-
rience in delivering housing services for individuals with a develop-
mental or intellectual disability.

Lastly, the bill requires OPWDD to include housing counseling services
in the statewide comprehensive plan required by § 5.07 of Mental Hygiene
Law. The statewide comprehensive plan will include information related
to progress implementing and the effectiveness of housing counseling
services, and any other information deemed appropriate by the commis-
sioner.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Appropriate housing is necessary for people to live stable, healthy
lives. For people with disabilities, the right housing opportunity can
lead to the overall well-being and success of a person and allows that
individual to become an active part of their community. New York's Medi-
caid Redesign Team has found that stable, sustainable housing leads to
improved health outcomes.

Unfortunately, there are obstacles to finding appropriate housing for
people with disabilities. Identifying the right housing can oftentimes
be complex. Finding affordable and appropriate housing for a person with
a disability in a state that is as diverse as New York can oftentimes be
a challenge.

In 2015, the New York State Association of Community and Residential
Agencies organized a Housing Task Force to study impediments to housing
for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.  Funded
through a Balancing Incentive Program (SIP) grant, the task force was
comprised of state and county officials, affordable housing developers,
educators, bankers, attorneys and service providers. One key finding of
the task force is that housing plays a critical role in a person's
development. The task force also determined that stability is key to
improving an individual's outcomes. New York is a state that is
geographically diverse and comprised of vast rural areas, large urban
centers and sprawling suburbs. I/DD providers are located in all regions
of the diverse state and deliver supports and services to the over
130,000 people with I/DD in many communities.

Not-for-profit provider agencies actively seek housing options for the
people they provide supports to. Unfortunately, the degree to which
agencies explore non-OPWDD funding sources varies. Seeking such housing
outside of the system is a specialty service and one that's not current-
ly funded. The task force also found that funding for housing is limited
and typically available for the more traditional housing opportunities
some of which are not always the best fit for a person seeking individ-
ualized opportunities. Non-OPWDD housing resources are available but
such funding sources are not easily identifiable, the various systems
are not easy to navigate, and knowing how to put the pieces of the hous-
ing puzzle together is complex and requires ample time, resources and
specialized experts to understand the nuances. Additionally, people with
disabilities, parents and family member are oftentimes unfamiliar with
the range of housing options and require assistance to identify appro-
priate settings.

Therefore, a growing need exists for housing counseling services to
assist people with disabilities the opportunity to assess their housing
needs and options, provide assistance to secure housing, and foster the
establishment of procedures and contacts to create and retain housing.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-20: S4014 Reported from Committee and committed to Finance
2017-18: A10732 referred to Ways & Means

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the April 1, 2022 provided that, effective
immediately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rule or regu-
lation necessary for the implementation of this act on its effective
date are authorized to be made and completed on or before such effective
date.
